source.excerpt: Yes, but I have something he will never have
trail: Bogle’s 18 May 2007 Georgetown address opens with a story of Heller and Kurt Vonnegut at a wealthy host’s party, using “Yes” and “he will” in the reply.
In his inspected 2009 address, Bogle explicitly says he is summarizing Vonnegut’s short poem, so this is a chain of retellings rather than an independent transcript of Heller speaking.
Wikiquote supplies the “Yeah … he’ll” version through a 2007 Money reference. No original recording or contemporaneous record of the party conversation was established; no poem is reproduced here.

author.bio: Joseph Heller (1923–1999) was an American novelist and screenwriter. His debut novel Catch-22 (1961) satirizes war and bureaucracy; its title became a familiar term for a self-defeating or contradictory predicament.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The anecdote contrasts a rich host’s earnings with Heller’s sense that he already has enough. Bogle used the story to frame a commencement address about business values and limits on the pursuit of money. That later use gives the reply a clear circulation history, while leaving the exact words of the original private conversation uncertain.
